title: Probabilistic impact scorer and adaptive quiet-window for noisy alerts
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Adds a probabilistic impact scoring model and adaptive quiet-window feature to reduce alert noise while preserving high-impact signal. Includes metrics, dashboards and a simulation harness. Backwards compatible and off by default; opt-in via incident-bot config.
description: Context and motivation: On-call teams are overwhelmed by low-impact recurring alerts that consume cognitive bandwidth but do not represent material customer impact. This PR implements a probabilistic alert-impact scorer and an adaptive quiet-window mechanism that dynamically suppresses low-likelihood, low-impact repeats while preserving immediate escalation for high-impact signals. Key ideas: compute per-alert posterior impact probability by combining SLI deltas, error-rate magnitude, failing shard cardinality, and inferred customer-facing weight using a lightweight Bayesian prior and feature-normalization; use a short-term adaptive quiet-window that grows with repeated low-impact occurrences and decays faster when upstream error fraction increases; provide explicit safety gates (minimum retention count, per-service opt-out, manual override) and an audit trail so suppressed events are recorded and can be surfaced to oncall during post-incident reviews. What changed: 1) core scorer service: incident-bot/score/prob_impact.py - new scoring pipeline with pluggable feature transforms and a small distilled model for on-device inference; 2) suppression controller: incident-bot/suppression/adaptive_window.go - adaptive state machine that tracks occurrence history and computes suggested suppression durations with exponential backoff and jitter; 3) telemetry hooks: metrics added (incidentbot.prob_impact.score, incidentbot.suppression.duration_suggested, incidentbot.suppression.suppressed_count) and traces for decision paths; 4) config and rollout: incident-bot/config/schema.yaml adds feature flags and per-service thresholds; 5) simulation harness: tools/alert-sim/runner.py to run replay experiments against historical alerts to estimate false-suppress/false-pass tradeoffs; 6) console: small UI cards and dashboard panels wired in observability-pack/dashboards/quiet_window.json to visualize suppression churn and missed-high-impact regressions; 7) docs: a single-page operational guide with examples and escalation flows. Safety and rollout: feature is opt-in per-service, default off. CI includes integration tests that replay a small anonymized alert history to validate suppression decision boundaries and a canary job that runs the scorer in a constrained environment. Checklist: - [x] core scoring algorithm implemented with unit tests - [x] suppression state machine with persistence and TTL handling - [x] telemetry events and dashboards wired - [x] simulation harness and a first-pass replay recorded - [x] documentation and runbook additions - [x] reviewers addressed comments and edge cases - [x] feature gated behind config flag and rollout steps documented Related work: follows discussion in ENG-1245 and complements the noisy-alert attenuator in slo-toolkit; incident where noisy cache-miss alerts flooded a pager on 2025-11-07 motivated the design. Links: Linear ENG-1245, replay artifacts: tools/alert-sim/recordings/2025-11-07.json. Testing notes: unit and integration suites passed locally; CI initially failed a flakey tracing test and was rerun; final CI green. Migration notes: no DB migration required beyond adding an optional suppression table (non-blocking), default retention 7d. Operational play: oncall can toggle suppressions per-service, and a manual "resurface" action sends suppressed events into a briefing queue. Rollout plan included in the PR description below.

notes_for_ops: Feature is behind 'adaptive_quiet_window' gate in config/schema.yaml; start with sample config in docs/oncall/quiet-window-runbook.md. Suggested canary: enable for a single low-impact service for 48h, validate suppressed_count and missed_high_impact metrics, then expand to platform team services. Emergency opt-out: set suppression.mode=off for service or toggle global flag.
rollout_plan: 1) enable opt-in for alpha team and monitor for 48h; 2) run replay-sim with recent 30d data to calibrate priors; 3) expand to platform-level services with 7d retention; 4) iterate on feature weights if missed-high-impact > 0.5% over baseline; 5) GA after two 2-week canaries showing stable metrics.
changelog_summary: Introduces adaptive quiet-window and probabilistic impact scoring to suppress low-value repeated alerts; opt-in, observable, and reversible.
audit_log_notes: Suppressed events are recorded to incidentbot.suppressed_events (append-only) with reason and score; resurface actions write to briefings queue with original context.
